# Week of May 28, 2026

This week answered three open questions from the May 7 entry: which preprocessing actually works for
merged multi-platform training, whether a cohort indicator helps, and whether to standardize on LB or
YFB. It also tested DeSurv-aligned gene selection as a replacement for plain variance filtering.

## Method updates

- **18-configuration preprocessing benchmark (5/27).** Compared 5 preprocessing strategies (joint
  quantile normalization + rank transform, per-platform z-standardization, joint QN without rank
  transform, joint z-standardization, log-only) across LB and YFB, with and without a cohort
  indicator, on merged TCGA+CPTAC ($n=273$, 5-fold CV, biological floor $K\geq3$).
- **DeSurv-aligned gene selection (5/28).** Replaced variance-only gene selection with a combined
  mean+variance rank computed per-platform before normalization (DeSurv's own approach), keeping the
  top 3,000 genes per cohort (2,064 after intersection, vs. 2,000 before).

## Results updates

**Critical finding: preprocessing is not a free choice.** 10 of the 12 non-per-platform
configurations collapsed to $\hat\beta=0$ for every factor. Only **per-platform z-standardization**
consistently recovers non-zero survival coefficients — without it, the top singular vectors of the
merged matrix capture the RNA-seq/proteomics platform contrast rather than biology, and the survival
update has nothing real to latch onto.

**Cohort indicator is situational, not a free win.** It absorbs the platform offset when preprocessing
hasn't already removed it (+0.020 for LB with joint QN — meaningfully helpful there), but is neutral
to harmful once per-platform z-standardization is already in place (+0.004 for LB, −0.013 for YFB,
where at low $K$ it competes with the 2 biological factors for variance). Recommendation: keep it
available as a robustness option for LB when per-platform preprocessing can't be guaranteed, but
exclude it from the primary YFB configuration.

**DeSurv gene selection improved external concordance in both model families:** +0.012 for YFB (D4 vs.
the earlier per-platform-only D2), +0.006 for LB (D3 vs. D1). YFB also outperformed LB on the same
DeSurv gene set by +0.014 (D4 vs. D3) — the two effects are additive. Every one of the 5
configurations tested (D1–D5) converged to exactly **2 active survival factors** regardless of how
many factors were requested (K ranged 3–8), with one adverse-direction and one protective-direction
program every time — the same 2-factor structure keeps showing up no matter how we slice the
preprocessing, which is a good sign it's a real property of the data rather than a fitting quirk.

| Config | Model | Gene selection | Cohort ind. | K | K_eff | Mean external C |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| D4 (recommended) | YFB | DeSurv, 2,064 genes | No | 7 | 2 | 0.636 |
| D3 (sensitivity) | LB | DeSurv, 2,064 genes | No | 7 | 2 | ~0.630 |
| D5 | YFB | DeSurv, 2,064 genes | Yes | 8 | 2 | 0.614 |
| D2 (prior baseline) | YFB | Variance only, 2,000 genes | No | 3 | 2 | 0.624 |
| D1 (prior baseline) | LB | Variance only, 2,000 genes | No | 3 | 1 | ~0.624 |

*(D4's 0.636 is the number as understood this week; a train/test preprocessing bug found later, on
7/15, revises this down to 0.627 — see that entry. Kept here as the historical record of what we
knew at the time.)*

## Relevance of new findings

This is the week the recommended configuration actually converges: **YFB, DeSurv-aligned gene
selection, per-platform z-standardization, no cohort indicator, $K=7$.** It beats the alternatives for
concrete, understood reasons (platform-scale collapse avoided, gene selection matches DeSurv, YFB's
exact scoring beats LB's OLS approximation) rather than by grid-search luck — every one of the 18/5
configurations tested has an explanation for why it does or doesn't work, which is what makes this
choice defensible going forward rather than just "the biggest number in a table."

## Open items to address

- Pathway enrichment on D4's 2 active factors (Factor 3 adverse, Factor 7 protective) — the main
  interpretability task left before the biology story can be told.
- Compare patient loadings on the 2 active factors to Moffitt subtype scores in TCGA to check
  concordance with classical vs. basal subtypes.
- YFB's point-normal prior still returns C=0.5 for all K in cross-validation — open issue, normal
  prior remains the default.
- Cohort indicator may earn a second look once training extends past 2 platforms.
